user.title: Connect to Crafty Controller
user.description: Enter the address of your Crafty Controller panel and an API token. Create the token in Crafty under Panel Config → Users → Edit → API Keys, then click “Get A Token”. See the README for the exact permissions each feature needs.

data_description.api_token: The long string shown by “Get A Token”. Needs at least the Logs permission for player tracking.
data_description.verify_ssl: Leave off if Crafty uses its default self-signed certificate.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Crafty Controller
reconfigure.description: Change the Crafty address, token or certificate setting. Leave the token blank to keep the current one.

reauth_confirm.title: Crafty token expired
reauth_confirm.description: Crafty at {url} rejected the saved API token. Create a new key under Panel Config → Users → Edit → API Keys, click “Get A Token” and paste it here.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Crafty. Check the address and port (default 8443).
error.ssl_error: SSL certificate check failed. Turn off “Verify SSL certificate” for Crafty's self-signed certificate.
error.not_crafty: That address responded, but not like a Crafty Controller 4 panel.
error.unknown: Unexpected error, see the Home Assistant log.

abort.already_configured: This Crafty panel is already set up.

data_description.player_source: Bedrock 1.26.60+ servers can't be pinged, so Automatic reads joins and leaves from the server log for them.
data_description.servers: Leave empty to include every server, including ones you create later.

options.auto: Automatic (log for Bedrock, Crafty ping for Java)

send_command.name: Send console command
send_command.description: Sends a command to a Minecraft server's console through Crafty, as if typed in the Terminal tab.

device_id.name: Server
device_id.description: One or more Minecraft server devices.

command.name: Command
command.description: Console command without the leading slash, e.g. say hello or gamemode creative @a.
